rationale: Both reviews are grounded and well-evidenced, cover the enum/test-coverage points implicit in the ground truth, and add plausible unique findings (concurrency race in X, default-level footgun in Y). X's blocker finding is a near-exact match to the real historical incident: it names the five specific pre-existing hardware tests (with line numbers) that sleep(level=2) then wake_up() and would now hit the new NotImplementedError, which is precisely the over-strictness that broke merge CI per issue #4905 — a direct gap_hit. Y's related finding (default level=2 bricking the common path) is adjacent but frames it as a default-parameter footgun rather than identifying that existing tests/CI already exercise and would break on the newly guarded path, so it only partially reaches the gap. X's citations (grep line numbers, worker-side implementation contradicting the blanket ban) are also more concretely actionable.
